explanation: Option A is correct because entity integrity requires the primary key ProjectID to be non-null, and referential integrity requires the foreign key SponsorID to be either null when optional or equal to an existing referenced SponsorID. B and D violate entity integrity by allowing a null primary key. C violates referential integrity by allowing SponsorID values that do not exist in Sponsor.

options.text: ProjectID must be non-null, and SponsorID must be either null or an existing SponsorID value
ProjectID may be null if SponsorID matches an existing SponsorID
ProjectID must be non-null, and SponsorID may be any integer whether or not it exists in Sponsor
SponsorID must be non-null, but ProjectID may be null

prompt: A company stores projects in Project(ProjectID PRIMARY KEY, SponsorID INT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (SponsorID) REFERENCES Sponsor(SponsorID)). Which rule always preserves both entity integrity and referential integrity when inserting a project row?
reviewConcept: To satisfy both rules, primary-key values must be non-null and foreign-key values must be null only when allowed or else match an existing parent key.
